rulings.challenge_claim: The curly-quoted WEB citation for web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2 substitutes a straight apostrophe for the source's curly apostrophe, breaking byte-verbatim fidelity inside an otherwise well-grounded wasf-boundary claim.
rulings.grounds: The byte fact is confirmed; the framing and the scope are both wrong. Exact-substring test (no punctuation normalisation) of every curly-quoted WEB span in this cluster's seven rows against the staged WEB verse text: 10 spans tested, exactly 3 fail, all three by U+0027 standing where the source carries U+2019 - web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2 (source reads “prince’s daughter!”), web:Song.7.10 = oshb:Song.7.11 (“I am my beloved’s.”) and web:Song.7.11 = oshb:Song.7.12 (“Let’s go out into the field.”); the other seven spans are exact, including both of P02-012's and the long adjuration span at web:Song.8.4. So the defect is real but it is a THREE-SITE CLASS, not the single site the challenge frames. Severity correction: the campaign's WEB-verbatim arm is punctuation-normalised BY DESIGN (it is a gloss-as-WEB detector) and returns GREEN on all seven rows, and the mandatory register rule governs the ENCLOSING curly double quotes plus an inline web: ref in the same field, which every row here satisfies; the straight apostrophes inside the row's own Hebrew glosses are correct under the same rule. Tier: English-witness transcription fidelity - no Hebrew tier, no boundary warrant and no evidence ref moves on this finding.
rulings.remedy: One sweep, not three spot fixes: in boundary_rationale of P02-010, P02-013 and P02-014 replace U+0027 with U+2019 inside the curly-quoted WEB spans ONLY, leaving the straight apostrophes in the straight-quoted Hebrew glosses untouched. Test the cure must pass: an exact-substring test with punctuation normalisation DISABLED of every curly-quoted span in the revised rows against the staged WEB verse text - the test that returned 3 failures out of 10 here must return 10 of 10.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row states an arithmetically false numbering-space identity for the offset zone and leaves its front seam - the book's crosswalk seam - uncited, while the tier-1 gender marker its own signal key rests on runs unbroken across that cut.
rulings.grounds: Defect 1 is the load-bearing one and is confirmed: boundary_rationale reads '(WEB ch 7 = MT 7:2-7:6)'. Re-derived from the crosswalk in both directions - WEB ch 7 holds 13 verses and maps to MT 7:2-7:14 (MT ch 7 holds 14); MT 7:2-7:6 is only this row's own span (= WEB 7:1-7:5). A false chapter-level identity written in the one zone where dual discipline binds hardest, and it is invisible to the machine arms: the structured-ref arithmetic and the prose-pair arm both return GREEN on this row because the falsehood is a CHAPTER-level statement in prose. Defect 2 upheld in part and refined: the front neighbour web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1 appears in no evidence ref and in no prose, while the 2fs addressee marker IS continuous across that cut - oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 carries שׁ֤וּבִי four times (2fs imperative) and וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (2fs suffix), byte tier, and the row's own opener oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1 reads מַה יָּפ֧וּ with 2fs פְעָמַ֛יִךְ, so only the suffixed-body-part sub-class begins at MT 7:2 and a tier-1 address marker straddles the front seam undisclosed. REFINED: OL's supporting sub-claim that the praise-exclamation CONSTRUCTION also straddles the cut does not hold at its own digit - the skeleton sweep OL cites (3 verses: MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6) is a sweep of the mah-plus-yod-pe opener, an object that EXCLUDES MT 7:1; מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ at MT 7:1 shares only the bare interrogative particle, which is not that device. Right digit, wrong count-object for the straddle claim. Defect 3 upheld at low: מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר at oshb:Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.5 is the anarthrous member of the melek-lexeme set (independently re-swept: 5 verses, MT 1:4, 1:12, 3:9, 3:11, 7:6), and the row's straight-quoted byte-tier gloss 'the king is held captive' imports the English witness's definiteness. Tier-4 audit only, never evidence in either direction: OL's note that the uncited front seam coincides with a WEB [SPEAKER] apparatus site is correctly labelled and correctly excluded from the warrant. Convergence: LF's item on this row is a DISTINCT defect from OL's - no overlap.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the false parenthetical and state either the span-level relation already carried in boundary_evidence_refs or an arithmetically correct chapter statement (WEB ch 7 = MT 7:2-7:14). Test: re-derive the chapter mapping with the crosswalk in BOTH directions and confirm the 13/14 verse counts before any chapter-level identity is written - the arithmetic that killed the original, and one no validator arm performs on prose, so a GREEN suite re-run does not certify this cure. (2) boundary_evidence_refs: add the front-seam pair web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1, and disclose in boundary_rationale that the 2fs addressee marker runs ACROSS the front cut while only the suffixed-body-part run begins at oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, with spliced byte-tier forms on both sides. Test: the front-seam claim must quote a gender-marked form on both sides of the cut, not on one. (3) Re-cut the MT 7:6 gloss to the anarthrous bytes.

rulings.challenge_claim: strongest_rejected_alternative engages only the weaker back-fold rival and omits the stronger, undisclosed forward-fold rival into the second wasf run.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative addresses only attachment to the preceding wasf; the forward fold into the second wasf run (web:Song.7.7-Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.8-Song.7.10) is engaged nowhere in the row. LF's device object re-derived independently rather than reproduced: the skeleton sweep of the praise-exclamation opener returns exactly 3 verses - MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6 - so מַה יָּפִית֙ וּמַה נָּעַ֔מְתְּ in the row's own verse shares its opener formula with the FIRST wasf's opener מַה יָּפ֧וּ (skeleton tier, named as such), which makes 'this verse OPENS a wasf run' the strongest available rival rather than the back-fold the row declined. Aggravating and found independently here: the warrant offered on both sides is that 'the mechanically derived run ends at MT 7:6' - the derived wasf zone is a staging signal and is barred as row evidence, so the one rival the row does engage is refused on a non-evidentiary ground. NEW FINDING (neither primary): boundary_evidence_refs on this one-verse row carries its own verse and the PRECEDING span only - the forward neighbour web:Song.7.7 = oshb:Song.7.8 is absent, so the very seam the challenge concerns is uncited, and the row's seam citation is asymmetric. LF's tier-3 absence citation (no PE and no SAMEKH between MT 6:10 and MT 7:11) re-verified against the parashah inventory and correctly handled - absence is never counterevidence, and LF says so explicitly.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the back-fold sentence with the forward-fold rival (this verse as the opening exclamation of the wasf run at web:Song.7.7-Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.8-Song.7.10), declined on argued bytes; delete the derived-run appeal from the rationale and from the rival sentence alike; boundary_evidence_refs: add web:Song.7.7 = oshb:Song.7.8. Test the replacement warrant must pass - the test that killed the original: it must dispose of the 3-verse skeleton-tier opener formula (MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6) on bytes alone, with no appeal to the mechanically derived run and no appeal to a speaker heading.

rulings.challenge_claim: The single-verse cut is carried by a voice-shift signal key, but the bytes show no shift at all - same speaker, same 2fs addressee across MT 7:6-7:8 - and the vocative construal that supplies the only other warrant is undecidable on the staged evidence.
rulings.grounds: The bytes are exactly as stated and the mislabel is real; the granularity framing over-reaches. CONFIRMED: oshb:Song.7.7 = web:Song.7.6 reads מַה יָּפִית֙ וּמַה נָּעַ֔מְתְּ - both perfects 2fs, carrying no final qamats where the 2ms counterparts would - flanked by 2fs body-part suffixes at oshb:Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.5 (רֹאשֵׁ֤ךְ עָלַ֨יִךְ֙) and oshb:Song.7.8 = web:Song.7.7 (קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙), byte tier, with both witnesses reading one continuous address. No speaker change and no addressee change sits at either seam, so the observed_substrate_signals key voice_shift.transitional_address_exclamation is byte-false: the field contract requires the key to name the signal class actually consulted, and the class consulted here is a wasf form-class edge. REFINED (framing and severity): the conclusion that the cut is what the granularity rule forbids does not survive its own consequences - read that way the rule would equally forbid the two flanking wasf rows, which sit inside the SAME single voice; the owner's vocabulary makes wasf bounds writer-argued form-class seams (openers, closures, addressee shifts), so a wasf-to-non-wasf edge inside one voice is a licensed boundary. What is curable is the driver LABEL and the missing continuity disclosure, not the existence of the cut. Second defect upheld at low: 'as a vocative' for אַהֲבָ֖ה בַּתַּֽעֲנוּגִֽים is decided rather than held - the noun is anarthrous, no morphology layer is staged, and the rival construal (love as the exclamation's subject) stands on the same bytes, so the vocative reading tracks the English rendering and must be disclosed as held. Independently re-derived and CLEAN: the row's digit claim 'one of the ten ahavah-noun sites (sweep: 10 verses)' - the bare skeleton sweep returns 15 verses, less the 5 she-ahavah relative-verb formula verses (MT 1:7, 3:1-4), leaving 10 noun sites including MT 7:7; object correctly split, digit correct. Convergence: LF's item and OL's are DISTINCT defects at the same seam - a missing rival versus a byte-false driver key - and together they show one underlying weakness, that the isolation rests on a staging signal plus a mislabelled key rather than on bytes.
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the voice_shift.* key with a wasf form-class key (e.g. wasf.form_class_edge_non_body_part), and re-open every field the contract makes dependent on a driver swap - boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type, confidence. boundary_rationale must state that speaker and 2fs addressee are CONTINUOUS across both seams, with spliced byte-tier forms from oshb:Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.5, oshb:Song.7.7 = web:Song.7.6 and oshb:Song.7.8 = web:Song.7.7, and must hold the ahavah vocative construal open instead of asserting it. Test the cure must pass: no voice_shift.* key may stand on this row unless a gender-marked form or an attested formula anchor CHANGES at one of its seams - the test the original key fails.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's own last verse carries her address-word for him, undisclosed, contradicting the row's single-voice attribution and binding that verse forward into the mutual-belonging refrain across the row's back seam.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on bytes. oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 - the row's own final verse - reads הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים (byte tier); dodi is her word for him and is a tier-1 address vocabulary under the owner's moderate voice-attribution policy. The row is typed wasf_poem on the single signal key wasf.body_part_run_2fs_suffixes and quotes only that verse's closing three words דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים, never the dodi clause. Both witnesses carry it - WEB renders “that goes down smoothly for my beloved” at web:Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.10 - so this is not an apparatus artefact. The token then repeats immediately across the back seam as אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י at oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, and the independent skeleton sweep of that exact form returns 5 verses (MT 5:5, 5:6, 6:3, 7:10 = WEB 7:9, 7:11 = WEB 7:10): a byte-true tier-1 device straddling the row's own seam, which argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed. The row's back-seam warrant instead rests on imagery class plus 'matching the mechanically derived wasf boundary exactly', a staging signal barred as row evidence. REFINED sub-claim: the inference that the voice turn therefore sits INSIDE oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 is a construal the staged evidence cannot decide - no morphology layer is staged and both witnesses admit either the man taking up her word or her interjection - so it is held, not adopted. CONVERGENCE, and the decisive one in this cluster: LF SUPPORTED this row, certifying that both WEB quotes are byte-verbatim and that the live forward rival is correctly engaged, and LF's own evidence field quotes the closing run of oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 IN FULL, dodi clause included, without flagging it. The two primaries are not addressing the same defect: LF found none, and LF's support is itself defective. Tier-4 audit only, never evidence: OL's note that the chosen back seam coincides with a WEB [SPEAKER] apparatus site before web:Song.7.10 = oshb:Song.7.11 is correctly labelled non-evidential and is recorded solely as an audit against heading-leaning at the one seam where the row's own Hebrew runs the other way.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale must disclose the dodi token at oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 with a spliced byte-tier form, state how the unit's voice attribution survives a token of the OTHER address vocabulary standing inside its own span, and disclose the repetition at oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10 as cross-seam cohesion; strongest_rejected_alternative must decline the forward extension without the derived-run appeal; device_notes must name the swept object precisely (dodi-exact, not dod-family) wherever a dod digit is used. Test the cure must pass: delete the derived-run sentence and the revised back-seam warrant must still stand, and it must dispose of the 5-verse skeleton-tier chain of that exact form across the seam - the two supports the original never faced.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: a verbatim-quote apostrophe defect combined with an unengaged epigram_unit rival for this one-verse formulaic mutual-belonging declaration. OL: every claim in the row verifies byte-for-byte, but its forward seam is argued by nothing except a tier-3 mark while the dod chain and her continuing first-person voice run straight through both of its edges undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects, not one; OL's is the substantive one and is upheld, LF's splits. OL upheld: the forward seam oshb:Song.7.11 | oshb:Song.7.12 (= web:Song.7.10 | web:Song.7.11) is supported in the row by the setumah and by nothing else. Re-verified independently: the parashah inventory does carry SAMEKH at MT 7:11 under the claimed type, MT-keyed, and the row discloses it as single-witness - but in the Writings that layer is tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver. Across the cut oshb:Song.7.12 = web:Song.7.11 opens לְכָ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ - same speaker, same dodi vocative - so no tier-1 marker sits at the forward seam, while the FRONT seam, which the row argues from imagery class and the derived run, is the one that actually carries tier-1 markers: אֲנִ֣י plus לְדוֹדִ֔י plus an attested refrain anchor, against the man's 2fs wasf address at oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9. The row argues the seam that does not need arguing and leaves driverless the one that does. Cross-seam disclosure is absent: a dod-lexeme token stands in each of MT 7:10, 7:11, 7:12 and 7:14 with the defective דֹּדַ֖י at MT 7:13 (= WEB 7:9, 7:10, 7:11, 7:13 and 7:12). OL's 'five consecutive MT verses' is arithmetically right but its object is blended - the 28-verse dod-family sweep does NOT contain MT 7:13, which escapes it - so the honest object name is 'verses carrying a dod-lexeme token of any spelling'. LF splits: the apostrophe half is confirmed (web:Song.7.10 = oshb:Song.7.11 reads “I am my beloved’s.” in the source) but belongs to the three-site class already ruled on this cluster and cured by one sweep, not a second row defect. The epigram_unit half is REFUTED: that vocabulary value names self-contained aphoristic units, and these bytes carry a member of a 3-site attested refrain set quoted at its own attested shape, not an aphorism; the operative-category law permits another value where the row's bytes carry that form, and they do not. LF's supporting move - that the co-located setumah shadows bracket-closing and should have been weighed against unit_type - inverts the tier: the parashah layer may no more push a unit_type than it may drive a boundary. Policy note, deliberately NOT escalated: whether the hybrid rule's refrain-verses-close-units clause licenses ISOLATING a mutual-belonging refrain verse as the vocabulary licenses for the adjuration brackets is unsettled, but it does not need settling here, because the row's defect is an ordinary one either way.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: argue the FRONT seam from its tier-1 markers with spliced byte-tier forms (אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י at oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10 against the man's 2fs wasf address at oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9) and either supply an argued forward driver or record on the row that none exists; disclose the dod-lexeme chain straddling both seams with the object named per attested spelling; keep the setumah as corroboration only, single-witness, never as the forward warrant. BOUNDARY PROPOSAL ONLY, requiring explicit boss adoption and not an author-wave edit: if no forward driver can be argued, merge this verse with web:Song.7.11-Song.7.13 = oshb:Song.7.12-Song.7.14 as one unit opened by the refrain. Test the cure must pass: delete the setumah sentence and the forward seam must still stand on its own evidence - the support that is doing all the work in the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: an unscoped 'hapax' universal claim lacking the mandated digit-bearing sweep disclosure, plus the apostrophe defect. OL: the row names a Hebrew form that is not in its span - MT 7:13 reads the 1cs defective dodai, not a 2ms 'dodekha' - and its mandrake and cohortative labels are likewise off the bytes.
rulings.grounds: Upheld, and the severity rises above both primaries' medium: the lead defect is a Hebrew FORM named in row prose that the cited bytes do not carry, standing in the very row that owns the token, in the book whose signature hazard is dod-family blending. CONFIRMED (the form): oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12 reads אֶת דֹּדַ֖י לָֽךְ (byte tier). The attested token is דֹּדַ֖י - 1cs, no second-person suffix in the consonants at all - and both witnesses read the speaker's own possessive (WEB “There I will give you my love.” at web:Song.7.12 = oshb:Song.7.13), whereas device_notes calls it 'the defective-spelling dodekha token', a 2ms form absent from these bytes. Re-swept independently: the defective spelling returns exactly 4 verses (MT 1:2, 1:4, 4:10, 7:13 = WEB 1:2, 1:4, 4:10, 7:12); MT 1:2 and 1:4 carry a 2ms suffix and MT 4:10 the 2fs דֹדַ֖יִךְ, so MT 7:13 is the single member whose suffix runs the other way - wrong form and wrong direction of address in the row that argues who addresses whom. CONVERGENT, the SAME defect from both primaries: 'the mandrakes hapax' carries no scope and no digit. Re-swept: הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים returns 1 verse in this book (MT 7:14 = WEB 7:13); the staged evidence supports only a book-scoped digit, and 'hapax' is a universal claim requiring the adjacent digit-bearing citation that names object and unit. The automated universal arm does not carry 'hapax' in its claim vocabulary, so this class is reachable only by review - and both primaries reached it. CONFIRMED (the form labels): 'One sustained 1cs voice' and 'her single cohortative address' mis-state the run - the cohortatives in the span are first-person PLURAL, נֵצֵ֣א and נָלִ֖ינָה at oshb:Song.7.12 = web:Song.7.11 and נַשְׁכִּ֨ימָה֙ and נִרְאֶ֞ה at oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12, while the genuinely 1cs forms are אֶתֵּ֥ן and צָפַ֥נְתִּי; the automated universal arm independently flagged the word 'single' in that same sentence. The signal key voice_shift.1cs_cohortative_invitation inherits the error. LF's apostrophe half is confirmed (web:Song.7.11 = oshb:Song.7.12 reads “Let’s go out into the field.”) but belongs to the three-site class cured by one sweep.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: name the MT 7:13 token by its attested form - the 1cs defective spelling, spliced, byte tier, dual-cited oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12 - and state the direction of address it actually carries; scope the mandrakes claim to the book with its digit ('sweep: 1 verse in this book'). boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 1cs with 1cp for the cohortative chain and re-key observed_substrate_signals accordingly, re-opening rationale, rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence as dependents of the driver swap. boundary_evidence_refs: add the back-seam pair web:Song.7.13 = oshb:Song.7.14 | web:Song.8.1, currently uncited on both sides. Test the cure must pass: every Hebrew FORM named in prose must be re-spliced from its cited verse and re-collated at byte tier before the row ships - the check both 'dodekha' and '1cs cohortative' fail - and the mandrakes scope must carry a digit naming object and unit.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both primaries: the row cuts a continuous single-voice run at the WEB chapter 7|8 boundary with no tier-1 voice-shift marker at the cut and never engages the live merger rival with the preceding row (LF, high). OL adds an entirely uncited front seam, a quote/gloss parity break at 8:3, and an untiered recurrence claim that is not byte-identical to its counterpart.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENT - the two primaries name the SAME core defect, independently, and it is upheld on bytes. Across the cut neither speaker nor addressee changes: oshb:Song.7.14 = web:Song.7.13 closes דּוֹדִ֖י צָפַ֥נְתִּי לָֽךְ - her 1cs perfect under the dodi vocative of that same verse, with לָֽךְ the pausal 2ms, disambiguated by the in-verse vocative and by both witnesses (WEB “which I have stored up for you, my beloved.” at web:Song.7.13), not by the form alone - and oshb:Song.8.1 = web:Song.8.1 continues מִ֤י יִתֶּנְךָ֙, אֶֽמְצָאֲךָ֤ and אֶשָׁ֣קְךָ֔, 1cs verbs carrying 2ms object suffixes (byte tier). A wish particle is a construction, not a member of the tier-1 marker set (gendered forms, vocatives, attested formula anchors), so two rows BOTH typed lyric_address, both her voice addressing him, are cut apart with no qualifying driver - and neither row engages the merger: the preceding row declines only an internal epigram split, this row declines only the forward extension into the adjuration. Aggravating: the cut falls exactly on the WEB chapter 7|8 division, tier-4 metadata that is never boundary evidence; the parashah absence between MT 7:11 and MT 8:4 that LF cites is re-verified against the inventory and correctly handled as support for neither side. OL's added defects upheld at low. Quote/gloss parity: the run quoted at oshb:Song.8.3 is שְׂמֹאלוֹ֙ תַּ֣חַת רֹאשִׁ֔י וִֽימִינ֖וֹ, which ends on the right-hand word the gloss 'his left hand under my head' does not render and stops before תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי that governs it, so quote and gloss do not cover the same text. Untiered recurrence: the 8:3 echo carries no tier label and is NOT byte-identical to its counterpart - oshb:Song.2.6 reads תַּ֣חַת לְרֹאשִׁ֔י against תַּ֣חַת רֹאשִׁ֔י at oshb:Song.8.3, the lamed present in the earlier verse and absent here - making it a skeleton-adjacent echo that must say so. NEW FINDING (neither primary, and a class rather than a spot): that recurrence claim names no verse at all, and the same unanchored shape recurs at P02-013's device_notes. Because no verse is named, the ref-mirror arm stays GREEN and the claim never reaches boundary_evidence_refs - an unanchored cross-row reference evades the mirror check by construction, while the register rule requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored.
rulings.remedy: boundary_evidence_refs: add the front-seam pair web:Song.7.13 = oshb:Song.7.14 | web:Song.8.1; boundary_rationale must then disclose that speaker and addressee are continuous across that seam with spliced byte-tier forms on BOTH sides, and must either supply a tier-1 driver at the cut or record that none exists. Re-cut the 8:3 gloss so quote and gloss cover identical text. Tier-label the embrace echo, verse-anchor it to oshb:Song.2.6 and mirror that ref into boundary_evidence_refs, and run the same anchoring as a SWEEP across the part, starting with P02-013's unanchored mutual-belonging reference. BOUNDARY PROPOSAL ONLY, requiring explicit boss adoption and not an author-wave edit: merge web:Song.7.11-Song.7.13 = oshb:Song.7.12-Song.7.14 with web:Song.8.1-Song.8.3 into one maximal single-voice lyric_address. Test the cure must pass: remove the chapter number and the phrase 'fresh movement' and the cut must still stand - it must quote a gender-marked form or an attested formula anchor that CHANGES at the seam, which is exactly the test the original fails.

supported_sample.claim_checked: LF's supporting certification that this row's wasf bounds byte-match the derived zone at both edges and that both curly-quoted WEB spans are byte-verbatim. NOTE: no row in c05 was supported by BOTH primaries (LF supported one row, OL supported none), so the 10% sample is taken from the sole supported row and the support itself is what is re-verified.
supported_sample.notes: The two narrow sub-claims verify independently: the exact-substring test passes for “This, your stature, is like a palm tree” at web:Song.7.7 = oshb:Song.7.8 and “gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.” at web:Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.10, and the span edges do match the derived run - oshb:Song.7.8 = web:Song.7.7 opens זֹ֤את קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙ and oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 closes דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים, byte tier, with the +1 offset-zone mapping arithmetically correct. The load-bearing certification fails, however: LF's own evidence field quotes the closing run of oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 in full, which contains הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים - a tier-1 address vocabulary token of the OTHER voice standing inside a row typed as his praise poem of her - and certifies the row clean without flagging it. Independently re-derived: the token is present at byte tier and repeats immediately across the back seam (אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י at oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10; skeleton sweep of that exact form, 5 verses - MT 5:5, 5:6, 6:3, 7:10 = WEB 7:9, 7:11 = WEB 7:10).
